observation_kind: targeted current official NPD maintenance/delivery, Planning OpenAPI schema, time-stamped DTM/10m lineage and Terrain 50 national-format metadata checks; not independent bulk HTTP fetches
rules: HM Land Registry does not routinely update title plans or index polygons.
A customer query can trigger an update to a title plan or index polygon.
An incorrect adjoining registration noticed during another application can trigger an update.
A polygon found to be incorrect can trigger an update.
A sale of part can require land to be removed from a title and its index polygon.
Index polygons created, updated or deleted in production are uploaded overnight to the publication environment.
The overnight publication transfer uses Esri shapefiles.
Publication validation checks for zero-coordinate polygons.
Publication validation checks for zero-area polygons.
Publication validation checks for duplicate coordinate points within polygons.
Many polygon self-intersections are cleaned in the publication environment.
Polygons with zero area are removed from the publication environment.
Polygons with area below 0.1 square metres are removed from the publication environment.
A change-only update contains only the latest version when an index polygon changes several times.
HM Land Registry does not retain previous index-polygon versions for this delivery.
The National Polygon Dataset is published and updated monthly.
Access to the National Polygon Dataset is chargeable.
Access requires agreement to a dataset licence.
Users must create an account on the land-and-property data service before access.
Users must pay for the dataset before access is granted.
Updated files are available from the second working day of each month.
Licensed users receive the full dataset, change-only updates and validation files.
The dataset is delivered as CSV files.
CSV fields are separated with the comma character, ASCII 44.
All CSV fields are enclosed in double quotes, ASCII 34.
Blank fields are represented by double quotes with no character between them.
Files use UTF-8 encoding and place column-heading names in the first row.
The published Planning Data API specification uses OpenAPI 3.1.0.
The published API information reports version 0.1.0.
The OpenAPI information declares the MIT licence.
Entity search is exposed as a GET operation on /entity.{extension}.
Entity response suffixes are limited to JSON, HTML and GeoJSON.
The OpenAPI schema declares 'within' as the default geometry relation.
Entity search has a default result limit of 10.
Entity search enforces a minimum limit of 1.
Entity search enforces a maximum limit of 500.
The period filter supports all, current and historical values.
Organisation entity identifiers in the search schema have a minimum value of 1.
Entity-number filters in the search schema have a minimum value of 1.
A specific entity is retrieved with GET /entity/{entity}.{extension}.
The specific-entity endpoint requires an integer entity identifier.
Dataset listing is exposed as GET /dataset.{extension}.
Dataset response suffixes are limited to JSON and HTML.
The dataset-list include_typologies parameter defaults to true.
Validation-error objects require location, message and error-type fields.
The time-stamped DTM product is an archive of Environment Agency raster elevation data.
Site-specific LIDAR surveys in the time-stamped archive have been carried out since 1998.
Some areas, including the coastal zone, have been surveyed multiple times.
Time-stamped DTM data can be available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m or 2m resolution.
The time-stamped DTM is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal.
Surface objects are removed with bespoke algorithms and manual editing to produce the terrain surface.
The time-stamped DTM is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km ZIP files.
The data is in metres, referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
The time-stamped LIDAR data states vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The coordinate transformation used is specific to the survey time period.
The metadata catalogue identifies survey dates, product resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
The time-stamped DTM is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The time-stamped DTM metadata reports a quarterly update frequency.
The current metadata record reports no direct data services or area-of-interest resources.
An OSGM02-to-OSGM15 adjustment-grid ZIP is supplied as supporting information.
The 10m composite DTM is resampled from the 2m composite DTM.
The 10m DTM resampling uses bilinear interpolation.
The 10m DTM is supplied as a single GeoTIFF raster aligned to the OS National Grid.
The 10m composite DTM metadata reports an annual update frequency.
The full 10m product is supplied in a single named ZIP download.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied as a national GeoPackage file.
The GeoPackage single-file structure is designed to simplify transfer.
GeoPackage attribute names are not restricted to the shapefile ten-character limit.
The documented GeoPackage file-size limit is 140 TB, subject to the host file system.
GeoPackage supports raster, vector and database content.
The contour GeoPackage contains spot_height, land_water_boundary and contour_line layers.
The 2023 GeoPackage schema uses property_value instead of propertyValue.
GeoPackage type attributes use snake_case names such as spot_height_type and contour_line_type.
Contour vector tiles are supplied as one national MBTiles file.
Vector tiles use Web Mercator, EPSG:3857.
Contour, spot-height and land-water-boundary attributes are not mapped at zoom levels 0 through 8.
Those vector-tile layers and attributes are mapped at zoom levels 9 through 14.
OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
OS Terrain 50 provides metadata on a per-tile basis as well as for national product sets.
The XML metadata contains comments explaining the meaning of its tags.
The Esri auxiliary XML contains minimum, maximum, mean and standard-deviation height values.
The same auxiliary height statistics are supplied for every tile to support consistent colour ramps.
The default auxiliary styling can be disabled by deleting the file or adjusting min/max values in GIS software.
A full national supply of OS Terrain 50 grid tiles is documented as 157 MB compressed.
OS Terrain 50 ZIP compression is not encrypted.
